newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda sells $1.8 million of treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: Uganda sells $1.8 million of treasury bills.

text.p: The central Bank of Uganda sold 1.970 billion shillings ($1.8 million) of T-bills offered on the main 91-day category at the weekly auction, bank officials said on Thursday.
They said they sold the bills at an annualised yield of 11.776 percent, which was a 0.542 percent fall from last week.

They added that there was an oversubscription of 2.7598 billion shillings at the auction -- first oversubscription since mid-April. The prices ranged between 97.150 and 96.970 with a weighted average price of 97.064.
The Bank of Uganda invited tenders for 3.5 billion shillings of treasury bills on the main 91-day category only for the auction next Wednesday.
The bank introduced bearer treasury bills certificates on May 7, with a maturity structure of 91-, 182-, 273-, and 364-days.
Bank officials said the move was made in order to ease re-trading of the bills since the certificates bear no names.
But traders in treasury bills expressed worry over the certificates saying they were very open to fraud.
"These certificates are not signed so what happens when someone steals it and trades it?" one trader asked.
The bank acknowledged the problem but will only commit itself to maintaining a registry of the first holder of the certificates.
"Investors will retain the responsibility of preventing fraudulent acquisition of certificates by third parties subsequent to the initial issue of certificates," the central bank warned.
The certificates exist in denominations of 100 million, 50 million, one million and 100,000 shillings.
